text: On the night of May 11, 2022, professional cyclist Anna Moriah "Mo" Wilson was fatally shot by Kaitlin Marie Armstrong at a friend's home in Austin, Texas, shortly before 10 p.m. Wilson, born on May 18, 1996, in Littleton, New Hampshire, is the daughter of Eric and Karen (née Cronin) Wilson and sister to Matthew Wilson. She grew up in Kirby, Vermont, graduated from Burke Mountain Academy in 2014, and earned a Bachelor of Engineering (BE) from Dartmouth College in 2019. Raised in a family of athletes, Wilson developed a passion for cycling as a young girl and was a nationally ranked junior skier, becoming a gravel cyclist. Before her professional career, she worked as a demand planner for Specialized. Kaitlin Armstrong, born on November 21, 1987, grew up in Livonia, Michigan; she graduated from Stevenson High School in 2005, attended Schoolcraft College and Eastern Michigan University, and is a yoga instructor and licensed Realtor. Armstrong was in a relationship with professional cyclist Colin Strickland; they briefly separated in the fall of 2021, when Strickland began a romantic relationship with Wilson, which Armstrong later discovered. After reconciling with Strickland, Armstrong expressed a strong desire to kill Wilson, telling an anonymous tipster she had either recently purchased a firearm or was going to, and Strickland revealed he had bought two handguns for both of them. Police recovered two firearms from Strickland’s home, and a spent shell casing from Armstrong’s SIG Sauer P365 matched one found at the crime scene. Investigators also found evidence that Armstrong had visited a shooting range with her sister, Christine Armstrong, to learn how to use a firearm. Wilson was found dead with three gunshot wounds—two in the head and one in the chest—after she was already lying supine on the floor. Police identified Armstrong as a person of interest due to video surveillance showing her black Jeep Grand Cherokee arriving at the residence moments before the killing. Armstrong was taken into custody on an outstanding misdemeanor warrant for theft, made no statement to police when confronted about the video, and displayed an angry reaction when questioned about Wilson’s relationship with Strickland. A discrepancy between her date of birth in police records and the warrant led to her release on a technicality. An arrest warrant for first-degree murder was issued on May 17, 2022. Armstrong fled to Costa Rica, using her sister’s passport, assuming fake identities, and undergoing plastic surgery to change her appearance, spending 43 days at large before being apprehended on June 29, 2022, in a hostel in Santa Teresa, Costa Rica. U.S. Marshals noted her hair had been dyed and cut short, her nose bandaged, and there was discoloration around her eyes, which she claimed resulted from a surfboarding accident. Armstrong was arraigned on July 21, 2022, pleading not guilty to murder and held on a $3.5 million bond in Travis County Jail. After delays, the case went to trial on October 30, 2023. She lost her motion to suppress evidence from her custodial interrogation, which she claimed was illegally obtained due to lack of Miranda warning, and a federal charge of Unlawful Flight to Avoid Prosecution was provisionally dismissed as a routine motion under constitutional rights to a speedy trial. On October 12, 2023, Armstrong escaped from officers escorting her to a medical appointment and was re-apprehended after a brief chase; charges of escape causing bodily injury were later dropped. On November 16, 2023, after a trial before Judge Brenda Kennedy, Armstrong was found guilty of murder and sentenced to 90 years in prison with eligibility for parole after 30 years. She filed an appeal, which was denied, and is currently imprisoned at the Dr. Lane Murray Unit. On May 6, 2024, Wilson’s parents filed a civil wrongful death lawsuit against Armstrong seeking $1 million in damages, which they stated would ultimately be determined by a jury to include burial, funeral, and emotional damages, and to prevent Armstrong from profiting financially from the crime. On June 17, 2024, a judge ordered Armstrong to pay $15 million to the Wilson family. Three days after the lawsuit was filed, Armstrong emptied her bank account and transferred her assets to her mother, sister, and Colin Strickland, prompting Wilson’s family to file a separate lawsuit in July 2024 against Armstrong’s family and Strickland for fraudulent transfer. On June 15, 2024, Lifetime aired a television movie titled Yoga Teacher Killer: The Kaitlin Armstrong Story as part of its "Ripped from the Headlines" series, starring Caity Lotz as Kaitlin Armstrong, Kyle Schmid as Colin Strickland, and Larissa Dias as Moriah Wilson.
